summary: Computes a new buffer size as a2 plus the current capacity (this+4), allocates it via OperatorNewWithResultCheck, copies the currently stored data (this+8 bytes) from the old buffer into the new one, frees the old buffer, and stores the new pointer at this+0. Always returns 0.

local_names.a2: additional size requested on top of capacity
local_names.v6: out parameter receiving the new allocation

operations.description: Compute the new buffer size v3 as a2 + capacity (this+4).
Call OperatorNewWithResultCheck(v3, &v6) to allocate the new buffer of size v3.
Proceed only if the allocation returned success (non-zero); otherwise leave the old buffer untouched.
Copy the currently stored data (this+8 bytes) from the old buffer at this+0 into the new buffer.
Free the old buffer via FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Store the newly allocated buffer pointer into this+0.
Return 0 regardless of the allocation path.

unresolved: Capacity (this+4) is not updated after the reallocation, so the stored capacity becomes stale relative to the larger allocation; this may be intentional or a separate update site exists outside this function.
The constant return value 0 is odd for a successful reallocation; the caller's interpretation is unknown.
Sharing the same this+0/4/8 growable-buffer layout as MemcpyLikeWithRealloc (00587510) is plausible but not proven to be the same struct.
